plugin.requires_mcdr: Server Log Filter requires MCDR >= {version}: this MCDR has no InfoActionFlag, so the plugin is disabled. Please upgrade MCDR and try again.
language.unsupported: The configured language {value} is not supported; using {fallback} instead. Available values: {options}.
catalog.unreadable: [ServerLogFilter] Could not read the language file {path} ({error}); messages from it will show their raw keys.
summary.rules_enabled: Enabled {count} log filter rule(s); matches are hidden from the MCDR console only, the server log is unaffected
summary.no_rules: No filter rules are active (patterns is empty, or every rule failed to compile)
rule.catch_all: Filter rule matches everything, kept but please check: {pattern!r} -- it hides **every** line of server output, so the console looks like the server is not running. Usual typos are `.`, `.*`, `^`, `?`, `\w*`.
rule.duplicate: Filter rule is a duplicate, only the first one is kept: {pattern!r}
status.warned: {count} rule(s) (hides all output -- check for a typo like . / .* / ^)
status.duplicate: {count} rule(s) (listed more than once; only the first takes effect)
rule.compile_failed: Filter rule failed to compile, skipped: {pattern!r} ({error})
rule.dangerous: Filter rule risks catastrophic backtracking, skipped: {pattern!r} -- {detail}. This rule would stall MCDR's main thread on nearly every line; rewrite it as a plain substring or drop the nested quantifier and try again.
probe.too_slow: took {cost:.0f} ms on a {length}-character probe string (budget {budget} ms)
reload.carried: Carried over {count} hit(s) from the instance before the reload
reload.carried_session: ; the {count} hit(s) already counted this session are kept
session.report: Hidden {total} server log line(s) from the MCDR console this run (the server log file is unaffected)
help.logfilter: Server log filter (!!lf): show status / test a line / reload the rules
state.save_failed: Failed to write the filter statistics (state.json)
state.pruned_header: [ServerLogFilter] Cleared {count} rule statistic(s) from state.json (they are no longer in the configured patterns)
upgrade.title: [ServerLogFilter] Config updated: {count} new option(s) were added and written with their default values
upgrade.readme_hint: See the "Configuration" section of the README for what each one does.
broken.not_an_object: the top level should be a JSON object, but it is {kind}
broken.not_utf8: the file is not valid UTF-8 text (a common cause: it was saved as ANSI/GBK by an editor on Windows)
broken.backup_failed: [ServerLogFilter] The config file cannot be parsed, and backing it up to {file}.old failed too ({error}). The original file may have been reset -- please check.
broken.title: [ServerLogFilter] The config file cannot be parsed; it has been reset to the default config
broken.backup_line: - Your original file was saved as: {path}
broken.regenerated: - A new {file} was generated with the default values. Fix the content against your backup and put it back,
broken.reload_hint: or run !!logfilter reload once you have fixed it.
broken.cause_comma: Usual cause: every element of the patterns array needs a comma "," between them,
broken.cause_trailing: and there must be no trailing comma after the last one.
stale.title: [ServerLogFilter] Heads up: {count} filter rule(s) have matched nothing for {threshold} or more consecutive sessions
stale.cause_header: There are usually only two explanations:
stale.cause_regex: 1. The regex is wrong (spelling / case / escaping, or it does not match this server version)
stale.cause_gone: 2. The log line it targets is no longer produced (e.g. the upstream bug was fixed)
stale.advice_test: Advice: use !!logfilter test <a log line> to check whether the rule still matches;
stale.advice_remove: if it is useless, delete that entry from patterns,
stale.advice_threshold: if it is simply rare, raise stale_rule_threshold,
stale.advice_reset: or use !!logfilter reset to clear the counters and start observing again.
stale.note: (The reminder itself costs no performance -- it is only there to keep the config clean.)
status.no_rules: (no rules -- add some to patterns in the config file)
status.rejected: {count} rule(s) (bad regex or backtracking risk -- see the MCDR log)
status.tip: the server's own log is unaffected; hidden lines are still dispatched to plugin events.
help.permission: All of these need administrator permission (MCDR permission is not the same as being op in-game)
command.need_admin: Administrator permission required. MCDR reads permission from permission.yml, which is unrelated to being op in the game; have an admin run this in the MCDR console: !!MCDR permission set <your name> admin
help.entry_test: test whether a line would be hidden
help.entry_reload: re-read the config and apply it now
reload.pruned: ; cleared the statistics of {count} deleted rule(s)
test.stripped_note: (the [time] [thread/level]: prefix was stripped, so this tested the body that is actually matched)
config_doc.language: Message language. auto follows MCDR's current language setting (config.yml); zh_cn / en_us also work.
config_doc.patterns: The log lines to hide. A list of regexes; a line matching any of them is not shown on the MCDR console (the server's own log file is unaffected).
config_doc.log_matched_lines: When true, every hidden line is also written to the MCDR log, so you can confirm the rules really fire.
config_doc.report_on_server_stop: When true, log a one-line summary of how many lines were hidden, on server stop.
config_doc.warn_about_stale_rules: When true, a rule that matches nothing for several sessions is reported once, so dead rules can be cleaned up.
config_doc.stale_rule_threshold: How many consecutive idle sessions before the reminder. Set to 0 to disable it.
config_doc.validate_patterns: When true, patterns that would freeze the main thread (such as (a+)+$) are rejected at load time and reported in the log.
config_doc.pattern_probe_timeout_ms: Time budget (ms) for that check. A normal rule takes about 1 us, so there is normally no reason to change it. Values below 1 are treated as 1.
config_doc.announce_config_upgrade: When true, a plugin upgrade that fills in new config options also lists them in the console.
config_doc.announce_broken_config: When true, an unparseable config that gets backed up and reset is explained in the console, including the backup path.
